name: SF Tensor

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Pass-through + savings share (Terms v1.1, 2025-12-31, s.3.3): Total Amount Due = Actual Costs (underlying AWS/GCP/Azure etc. GPU instance + infra cost, spot where possible) + Savings Fee = 10% (annual spend up to $50k) / 8% ($50k-$200k) / 6% (>$200k, rolling 12 months) of Savings vs a Reference Price = average on-demand us-east price across AWS, GCP and Azure for equivalent instances. Customer-Managed Profile (BYOC): pay the cloud directly, SF Tensor invoices only the Savings Fee. Company-Managed Profile: prepaid credits required. No fixed $/GPU-h, $/vCPU-h or $/GiB-h; rates stay null (not free). Reference-price list page (/legal/prices) is 404 today.

plans.name: Savings-share (Terms s.3.3 / Model Foundry)
plans.note: Savings Fee 10%/8%/6% of savings vs AWS/GCP/Azure us-east on-demand average, tiered by rolling-12-month spend (<=$50k / $50k-200k / >$200k); custom % by written agreement. Company-Managed Profile must be pre-funded with credits (refundable minus transaction fees); jobs are not deployed and access can be suspended when credits run out. Customer-Managed (BYOC) profile invoiced in arrears for the fee only. Second engagement 'A research team and a model' is a fixed-price embedded-researcher engagement with compute billed separately; price not published. Service limited to US residents/US entities; EU residents excluded.

caveats: Live site sells Model Foundry (managed training, savings-share) and the Kernel Optimizer; the 2025 'Tensor Cloud' private beta is no longer in the navigation. /pricing and /legal/prices are 404. Published tariff = Terms s.3.3: underlying cloud cost pass-through + 10/8/6% of savings vs AWS/GCP/Azure us-east on-demand average. No fixed GPU/CPU/RAM rates; archived (Wayback, not live) price list showed 'Tensor Cloud $0.01 per GPU-hour' (v1.0, Nov 5 2025).
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

fleet.verification: Account application + onboarding; US residents / US-organized entities only; EU residents excluded; Company-Managed Profile requires pre-funded credits.
fleet.notes: Official site sells managed training outcomes and savings-share engagements, with planning/contact workflow. Claimed scale to 10,000 GPUs is not a new-account quota; underlying cloud/customer allocation remains relevant.

volume_shared.quote: STFS is our distributed read-through cache that fixes this: it makes an S3 bucket look like a filesystem, lets the cluster share cached ranges peer-to-peer and pulls those bytes over the fabric that is otherwise sitting idle.
volume_shared.note: Read-only: STFS is a FUSE mount of an S3 bucket shared by all training nodes ('It is a cache, not a filesystem ... refusing to fake rich write semantics'). Part of Model Foundry ('Training-native storage ... shared, cluster-local caching'); described in a blog post, not reference docs.

eu_data_residency.note: Service is contractually restricted to US residents/entities and explicitly excludes EU residents/entities.

isolation.quote: we're hiring a Member of Technical Staff for Sandbox Infrastructure to build the layer that makes it possible: a serverless GPU container service... customer workloads that require isolation, such as their RL rollouts, run on it too. We already do this on NVIDIA and AMD, including having rolled AMD GPU support in gVisor from scratch.
isolation.note: SF Tensor's own careers page describes the sandbox stack that isolates untrusted/customer GPU workloads (RL rollouts) as a gVisor-based container service; not a customer-facing docs page, so medium confidence. The customer-facing product itself deploys jobs onto AWS/GCP/Azure GPU instances (Terms s.3.1) rather than exposing this sandbox directly.

ssh.quote: Customer defines the job requirements, including the type and number of GPUs needed, and the Company deploys and manages the execution of such jobs on a cloud profile... The Company will deploy the job on the designated cloud profile and manage the execution of the workload.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. SF Tensor is a managed job-submission/training-outcome service (savings-share broker + embedded-researcher engagements), not an interactive VM/sandbox product; no docs describe direct SSH access to a machine.

volume_attach.quote: Customer submits job specifications through the platform, including workload requirements, GPU type and quantity, and preferred cloud profile.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No storage/volume API is documented; the product surface is job specs (GPU type/qty/cloud profile), not machine/volume management.

public_ipv4.quote: Train what doesn't exist yet... We handle everything between your idea and the silicon to let you iterate at the speed of light.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. SF Tensor runs training jobs, not networked services with exposed public IPs; no networking/ingress docs exist.

ingress_rules.quote: Train what doesn't exist yet... We handle everything between your idea and the silicon to let you iterate at the speed of light.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No inbound networking/ingress control feature is documented for this training-job service.

egress_allowlist.quote: Train what doesn't exist yet... We handle everything between your idea and the silicon to let you iterate at the speed of light.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No outbound-network allow/deny-list feature is documented; the product is a managed training-job broker, not a network-controlled sandbox.

guest_firewall.quote: you'll build and maintain GPU virtualization below the runtime, including gVisor work at the driver and ioctl level
guest_firewall.note: derived: the documented isolation mechanism for workloads is gVisor (a syscall-filtering sandbox), not a full VM/microVM with guest root, so unrestricted in-guest nftables/iptables control is unlikely and undocumented.

static_egress_ip.quote: Customer submits job specifications through the platform, including workload requirements, GPU type and quantity, and preferred cloud profile.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No fixed/static outbound IP feature is documented for this managed training-job service.

image_oci.quote: Training data, model checkpoints and container images live durably upstream, usually in an S3-style bucket.
image_oci.note: Training jobs are packaged/run as container images stored upstream of the fleet, consistent with launching jobs from a customer-supplied Docker/OCI image; not a dedicated docs page describing an image-push/registry API, so medium confidence.

max_session_h.quote: If a node fails, the run resumes from its last checkpoint on its own.
max_session_h.note: No fixed maximum session/run duration is documented anywhere (pricing, terms, or product pages); training runs are described as scaling to thousands of GPUs and resuming from checkpoints on failure, consistent with jobs running until completion/stopped by the customer rather than being cut off by a platform-imposed time limit.
